response: Yes, there is a correlation between humeral and glenoidal lesions in bony defects associated with chronic anterior posttraumatic dislocation of the shoulder. Studies have shown that the presence and severity of humeral head defects (such as Hill-Sachs lesions) are often related to the presence and severity of glenoidal lesions (such as Bankart lesions). The correlation suggests that the extent of the bony defect on one side of the joint is associated with the extent of the defect on the other side, which can impact treatment and outcome.
